about: World Economic Forum, Future of Jobs Report 2025: the jobs and skills employers expect to grow or decline by 2030, globally and for Malaysia, as printed in the report (text read from the PDF on 2026-10-31). The big-picture direction of the mock hiring-demand months (src/game/server/big-picture.js) reads it through the reviewed mapping src/data/config/wef-mapping.json. Directions only: the report's percentages are employer expectations, not hiring counts.

source.name: Future of Jobs Report 2025
source.basis: the perspective of over 1,000 leading global employers—collectively representing more than 14 million workers across 22 industry clusters and 55 economies

jobs.figure: Figure 2.2, Fastest-growing and fastest-declining jobs, 2025-2030 (top jobs by fastest net growth and net decline, projected by surveyed employers)
growing: Light Truck or Delivery Services Drivers
declining: Door-To-Door Sales Workers, News and Street Vendors, and Related Workers

skills.figure: Figure 3.4, Skills on the rise, 2025-2030 (net increase: share of employers expecting a skill to increase in use minus those expecting a decrease)
skills.quote: Also ranking among the top 10 skills on the rise are leadership and social influence, talent management, analytical thinking, and environmental stewardship. [...] However, a small net decline is anticipated in reading, writing, and mathematics.

malaysia.keyRolesMetric: net growth (%), roles most selected by organizations surveyed in Malaysia
